title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

errors: Notational slip. 𝓕 is written as ⊂ P(P_f(X)) and ∈ P(P(P_f(X))), but X is the support of one particular figure. The set of all figures must live in P(P_f(E)).

∂X_i here is Ẋ_i = ∪_{j<i}X_j, the union of the smaller strata. It is not the topological boundary in E. In general only Ẋ_i ⊂ frontier holds, so the notation can mislead unless a frontier condition such as (e) is imposed.
The inserted 'adh(X_i)' is redundant, since X_i is already closed.
Nonemptiness of int(X_i) needs the rareness of Ẋ_i in X_i. This follows from (b)+(c) via local finiteness, not from X_i ≠ ∅ alone. The text compresses this step.

ideas.what: Figure = locally finite family of closed strata, with rare proper inclusions and connected manifold open parts, plus closure under intersection (stratification indexed by a poset)
ideas.modern_name: closed poset-stratified space / stratification with frontier condition (Whitney–Thom–Mather style without regularity; Lurie's poset-stratified spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (1960s–70s); later Goresky–MacPherson, Lurie (HA App. A)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses tame topology and stratified structures informally; this precise definition does not appear there

ideas.what: Identifying a figure with its set of strata, F ∈ P(P_f(E)), and the ambient set 𝓕 of admissible figures
ideas.modern_name: set-theoretic encoding of stratifications; a 'site' or class of admissible stratifications

ideas.what: Total set Σ = ⨿_F Σ_F → 𝓕 of pairs (figure, stratum); together with p.3's sub-figure order and elementary figures, a fibred poset over the poset of figures
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck construction of F ↦ Σ_F; category of elements; poset of cells of a regular cell complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (fibred categories, SGA1) in general form
ideas.where_published: the general fibration formalism is in SGA1 VI; this specific use for 'shape models' appears unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a combinatorial/topological model of 'shapes' (modèles de forme, construits). The model is a family 𝓕 of closed stratifications of a (tame) space, with the total poset of strata fibred over 𝓕, intended as a foundation for tame 'analysis situs'. The 1986 program for building shapes combinatorially from such stratified data is not developed in the published literature under his name.
missed.quote: On se donne l'ens. des figures, noté 𝓕 ... L'ens somme Σ = ∐_{F∈𝓕} Σ_F → 𝓕
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a documented precursor of the poset-stratified/exit-path approach (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) and of o-minimal cell-decomposition combinatorics. It is relevant to historians tracing Grothendieck's tame-topology program after the Esquisse, though this page itself is foundational definitions only.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard definitions of a closed stratification and its poset of strata. The only distinctive feature is the beginning of a fibred structure over a set of admissible figures, aimed at a 'shape' theory. This is historically interesting but not mathematically surprising on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'est fermé dans X_i (par a), b), c))' rather than 'est fermé dans tous X_i, pour a) b) c))'.
'NB Dans le cas d'après' should read 'NB Dans le cas d'espèce, on a Σ_F ≃ F' (the struck-through continuation is illegible).
Left margin near Σ: 'Au lieu des Σ_F' / 'En place des Σ_F' – annotation that the points of Σ can be taken as pairs (F, X_i).
'f) X_i∩X_j est réunion de X_k' – probably 'réunion des X_k'.
Left margin item e) is a frontier-type condition involving X_i, X_j, ∂(X_j) and the open stratum X_i° (int X_i). It is partially illegible; the transcription's rendering is unreliable.
'𝓕 ⊂ 𝔓(𝔓_f)' – in the image the final expression is 𝓕 ∈ 𝔓(𝔓(𝔓_f(X))).
